clue.text: Provide food and support for a lover of greens

parts.note: to cater is to supply food for guests
a pillar is an upright support

explanation.surface: Someone feeding and standing by a partner who loves vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lover of greens' sounds like a vegetarian partner, but it is a leaf-munching larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva of a butterfly feeds greedily on green leaves, so it is fondly a lover of greens.

clue.text: Keen sort of house party

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic guest at a party in a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen in the sense of sharp or biting; acid house was a style of dance music behind raves.

clue.text: Former graduate comes up for a test

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An old university graduate returning to sit a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns MA to AM in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written assessment of knowledge, the everyday short form.

clue.text: Hidden danger that may trap miners

explanation.surface: A concealed hazard waiting for coal workers.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsuspected snag; literally a collapse in a mine shaft that could catch those working below.

clue.text: The temptation of misrule

parts.note: the pull towards bad government; misrule also hints at the word rule mis-arranged

explanation.surface: The appeal of disorder and anarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticement or attraction, a bait, read here also as the letters of rule jumbled.

clue.text: Paper is designed to inform

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper laid out to tell readers the news.
explanation.definitionFit: To give notice to someone, tell them the facts, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Where to see a naval ceremonial suit

definitions.text: Where to see a naval ceremonial suit

parts.words: Where to see a naval ceremonial suit
parts.note: the ceremonial part of a warship; suit also hints at a quarter of a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A guide to where officers parade in dress uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear upper deck of a warship, reserved for officers and ceremonies; a card suit is a quarter of the pack.

clue.text: Football club?

explanation.surface: A question about a soccer team.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer's formal name is association football; a society or league of members is a club.

clue.text: Signals and strikes the ball

explanation.surface: A snooker player giving signs and hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts given to actors are signals; in snooker or billiards one strikes the ball with a long rod, the verb sense.

clue.text: Mixed metaphors in Moliere play

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of the words beside it are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A critic complaining of muddled figures of speech in a French comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' turns METAPHORS plus IN into a new eleven-letter order.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a 1666 comedy by the French playwright, about a man who hates humanity.

clue.text: Trains a small number in Czechoslovakia

parts.note: BR stood for British Rail, the UK's old national railway
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Rail journeys counted in a central European country.
explanation.walkthrough: BR, British Rail, was Britain's state railway company. The definition names the place by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Moravia, part of the former Czechoslovakia, now in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Post date

explanation.surface: Sending something on a particular day.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or position held is a post; a fixed meeting time is a date.

clue.text: It provides outstanding images

parts.note: outstanding means standing out in three dimensions, not excellent

explanation.surface: Praise for a camera that takes excellent photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer that shows two pictures to give the illusion of depth, so images stand out.

clue.text: Caress a girl on the knee

parts.note: to pat is to touch gently and fondly
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone affectionately stroking a young woman's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the flat bone at the front of the leg joint, a loose anatomical synonym.

clue.text: A brief, for example, is for the defence

parts.note: e.g. is the brief, abbreviated, form of for example

explanation.surface: A barrister's case file prepared for the defending side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks legal but marks 'for example' as abbreviated to EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus, so a shield or guard.

clue.text: Airs composed by priest in Hebrew, perhaps

indicators.note: music composed is made up, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Tunes written by a cleric in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges the letters of 'Airs'. 'perhaps' tells you Hebrew is only one example: not every citizen of that state is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish citizen of the modern state, of whom a Hebrew speaker is one example.

clue.text: The Mohammedan world is hit

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike hard

explanation.surface: The Muslim world has been struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The faith, and by extension all the peoples and lands that follow it, the old term for Muslims.

clue.text: Document you take from a letter

explanation.surface: Words taken from correspondence you received.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter' here is not mail but a person who lets property, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental contract is a legal paper, and a tenant takes one from a landlord, someone who lets property.

clue.text: Feathered, they skim the water

parts.note: rowers feather their blades by turning them flat as they pass over the river, not birds

explanation.surface: Birds gliding low across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing blades are feathered, turned flat, so they skim the surface between strokes.

clue.text: Prepare to put out with the turn of the tide

indicators.note: the turn of the tide here means the word tide is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor getting ready to put to sea when the tide changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests sailing; it means publish. 'the turn of' reverses TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text is to prepare it for publication, putting it out.

clue.text: The latest thing in ties?

parts.note: ties are cup matches, not neckwear, and the last match of a knockout competition decides it

explanation.surface: A fashion question about the newest neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The deciding match of a cup competition comes last of all the rounds of fixtures.

clue.text: Fear led to new form of government

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Anxiety prompted a change in how the country was run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges FEAR and LED. The definition is loose: the answer describes a kind of government with powers shared by states.
explanation.definitionFit: A system in which states unite under a central authority while keeping some powers.

clue.text: Shy essayist gets a plant

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A timid writer is given a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' seems an adjective; it is the verb throw. Elia is Charles Lamb's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: A low garden flower, usually blue, popular in borders and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Old ones like this having little sense

indicators.note: like this tells us old ones must be rearranged into the word that names them

explanation.surface: Elderly folk who are a little foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' signals rearranging OLD ONES. The definition describes the people the answer names: simpletons, those with little sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles is old slang for fools, people with little intelligence.

clue.text: Book covering part of N Africa

explanation.surface: A travel guide to a North African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine goatskin leather used to bind books is named after the North African kingdom it came from.

clue.text: Club for those who like a bit of spice!

explanation.surface: A heavy weapon for people who enjoy hot food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for those who like a bit of' is link padding framing the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy staff carried in ceremony was once a war club; the dried nutmeg husk is a kitchen seasoning.

clue.text: They give a better interest

parts.note: a better is one who bets, and prices offered by the bookmaker give that punter an interest

explanation.surface: Savings accounts offering a higher rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' prices give a gambler a stake in a race.

clue.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

definitions.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

parts.words: If there's a man around, he's from the US
parts.note: set the words a man around this boy's name and the result describes someone from the US

explanation.surface: A remark that any man nearby must be American.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name; wrap the letters of a man around it and they spell a word for a US citizen.

clue.text: Fail to get the teacher's address

explanation.surface: Failing to learn where the teacher lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a form of address, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To not catch or hit something; a female teacher is called by this title in British schools.

clue.text: Honeymoon express, perhaps, may be held up

explanation.surface: A train carrying newlyweds that could be delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests a delayed train; it is the long gown tail lifted by bridesmaids.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway train for newlyweds, and the long trailing part of a wedding dress that attendants carry.

clue.text: Returns to bridge and dozes off

indicators.note: returns means the word for bridge is read back the other way

parts.note: a span is the arch of a bridge, or a bridge itself

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a card game and falls asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' seems to be the card game; it is a span. 'Returns' reverses SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Short sleeps are what one has when dozing, the third-person verb.

clue.text: Comprehensive horoscope for well-known performers in the show?

explanation.surface: Theatre publicity promising famous actors and a full astrological reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as words, a forecast cast from every star; as a phrase, a company of famous actors.
